question: Will Starbucks (SBUX) beat quarterly earnings?
reasoning: Starbucks reports Q3 FY2026 on July 29 against a consensus of ~$0.66 EPS, an aggressive +32% YoY implied bar set while the company is still in the heavy-investment 'Back to Starbucks' turnaround that has compressed margins and driven EPS misses in roughly 5 of the last 7 quarters (only Jan-2025 and the most recent Apr-2026 quarter beat). Comparable sales momentum is genuinely strong (Q2 FY26 comps +6.2%, three straight quarters accelerating) and Niccol's commentary is upbeat, which supports the top line, but the persistent pattern is that turnaround/labor investment spending causes EPS to miss even when revenue holds. Given that margin-driven miss history against a demanding +32% earnings bar, I see this closer to a coin flip than the market's optimistic 0.78.
evidence: Q3 FY26 consensus EPS ~$0.66 (Zacks), implying +32% YoY vs $0.50 prior-year quarter; revenue ~$9.44B (roughly flat YoY) — an aggressive earnings bar

Recent EPS record heavily skewed to misses during the turnaround: Q1 FY26 $0.56 vs $0.59 (miss), Q4 FY25 miss, Q2 FY25 miss; only Q2 FY26 ($0.50 vs $0.44) and Jan-2025 beat — margin pressure from 'Back to Starbucks' investment spending is the recurring cause
Strong operational momentum (global comps +6.2% in Q2 FY26, guidance raised to >5% comp growth) supports revenue but not necessarily bottom-line beat, since turnaround costs continue to weigh on EPS
Market prices ~0.78, but SBUX's poor recent EPS-beat rate against a high +32% consensus warrants a materially lower, near-coin-flip estimate

question: Will eBay (EBAY) beat quarterly earnings?
reasoning: eBay has beaten consensus EPS in at least the last five consecutive quarters (Q1'25 through Q1'26) and habitually sandbags its own guidance, giving a strong base rate for another beat around the ~7/28-7/29 report. I trim slightly below the market's 0.94 because current consensus (~$1.54) sits above the top of the company's own Q2 guidance range (~$1.46-$1.51), which raises modest miss risk, and I see no confirmed pre-announcement signal. Net view: a high-probability but not near-certain beat.

question: Will Coca-Cola (KO) beat quarterly earnings?
reasoning: Coca-Cola has an exceptionally consistent record of beating consensus adjusted EPS — including Q1 2026 ($0.86 vs $0.81), Q4 2025 ($0.58 vs $0.57), and Q3 2025 ($0.82 vs $0.78), with a trailing four-quarter average surprise of ~4.5% — and heads into the July 28 report ($0.92 consensus) with strong momentum after raising full-year EPS guidance on resilient demand and margin expansion. The main risk is definitional (KO frequently beats EPS but misses on revenue), so if 'beat' hinges on the top line the odds would be materially lower, but EPS-defined beats are the norm for these markets. I sit slightly above the 0.85 market price given the strength of the streak and Q1 guidance raise.
